opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max access is write (admin only if role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Analyst
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists Karen Alexander (E030) as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: HR (authoritative for employment status) records Karen Alexander (E030) as a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Analyst does not own it, so a full-time employee's maximum is write (admin is not allowed). The requested level (write) equals the maximum, so write is granted. The Security note lists her as a contractor, which conflicts with the HR employment record; I rely on HR for employment type.

The employee is Karen Alexander (E030), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes from HR and Security:
- HR says: full_time employee, Analyst, max write, recommend write
- Security says: contractor, basic security training, Analyst, max read, recommend read

The employment type is critical here. HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Which one to trust?

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Karen is an Analyst, so she doesn't own Source Code.

If full_time: max is write, request is write, grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read, request is write, grant read.

So the decision hinges on employment type. The HR agent says full_time; the Security agent says contractor.
